entries.reason: The National Library of Medicine describes rhamnogalacturonan I as a polymer of rhamnose and galacturonic acid units; an independent plant polysaccharide study confirms the repeating backbone. The source identifies rhamno- as rhamnose.

entries.meaning: monoamine oxidase type B inhibitor in drug names

entries.meaning: oxepin-containing tricyclic compound in drug names
entries.reason: The source assigns -oxepin to tricyclic compounds and lists doxepin; independent FDA product labeling identifies doxepin as a dibenzoxepin tricyclic compound. The drug-ending sense is narrower than all tricyclic compounds.

Wiktionary directly analyzes septavalent as septa- plus valent; Collins independently defines it as having a valency of seven.
WHO lists carbocisteine under -steine for mucolytics; a pharmaceutical dossier independently identifies carbocisteine and the stem.

The Paris Observatory astronomy etymological dictionary directly derives baryogenesis from baryo-, baryon, and genesis; an independent physics article uses baryogenesis in connection with baryon asymmetry.
WHO identifies -nakinra as the IL-1 receptor antagonist substem and lists anakinra; the FDA independently describes the drug as an IL-1 receptor antagonist.
Wiktionary lists massotherapy among terms with masso-; a historical English health text defines massotherapy as massage treatment.

WHO explicitly lists pitrakinra under the interleukin-4 antagonist substem -trakinra; an independent clinical study describes its action on IL-4 receptor signaling.
Wiktionary lists sacculocochlear under sacculo-; an independent medical dictionary defines it as relating to the sacculus and cochlea.

entries.meaning: curare-like neuromuscular blockers with rigid structure

The source lists drotaverine as an example of -verine; the Ethiopian drug regulator independently calls it a papaverine analogue with antispasmodic action.
The source identifies Swedo- as a Swedish combining form; an independent historical publication uses Swedo-Finnish to describe the Sweden–Finland kingdom.

WHO lists meprobamate under -bamate for tranquilizers of the propanediol and pentanediol groups; NIST identifies its propanediol structure and MedlinePlus independently describes its tranquilizer use.

entries.meaning: sodium-channel blockers and signal transduction modulators

Soil taxonomy identifies udi as the formative element for an udic regime; a North Carolina soil report independently defines Udifluvent as udic soil with fluvent conditions.

entries.meaning: carboline benzodiazepine receptor antagonists or agonists
entries.reason: WHO lists abecarnil under -carnil; an independent research paper characterizes it as a beta-carboline ligand at benzodiazepine receptors.
Collins analyzes visuospatial as Latin sight plus -o- plus spatial; American Heritage independently defines it in terms of visual perception of spatial relationships.

entries.meaning: quinoline benzodiazepine receptor agonists including partial and inverse agonists
entries.reason: WHO lists radequinil in the -quinil quinoline group; an independent Japanese pharmaceutical research report identifies radequinil as a partial inverse agonist at benzodiazepine receptors.
Collins analyzes mysophobia from the Greek word for filth and fear; the original medical article explains its coined name as fear of contamination.
Collins analyzes olfactometer as Latin olfactus plus connecting vowel and -meter; an early scientific account describes that exact instrument for measuring perception of odor.

entries.meaning: dopamine-derived dopaminergic agents used or investigated as cardiac stimulants (drug nomenclature)
entries.reason: WHO lists ibopamine in the -opamine group of dopamine-derived dopaminergic agents; independent pharmacology identifies it as a dopamine derivative investigated for cardiac effects.
An English cell-biology text analyzes phragmoplast from Greek phragma, hedge or enclosure; the research literature independently describes the structure forming a partition in cell division.
WHO identifies etilefrine as a -frine phenethyl sympathomimetic, and NLM independently classifies the same drug as a sympathomimetic adrenergic agonist related to phenylephrine.
WHO explicitly groups balsalazide under -salazide; NLM independently provides the compound’s phenylazosalicylic acid chemical name.
WHO directly assigns dibromsalan to -salan disinfectants; an international patent identifies the precise compound as a brominated salicylanilide used in disinfectant soaps.

entries.meaning: historical unofficial stem for phenethylamine-related bronchodilators
entries.reason: WHO documents -prenaline as the former unofficial bronchodilator stem and lists isoprenaline among corresponding names; the suffix is historical rather than a current universal synonym for -terol.
The English dictionary parses maltotriose as malto- plus triose; the LOINC biochemical description independently relates maltotriose to maltose by adding one glucose unit.
WHO explicitly includes cetirizine among -izine diphenylmethylpiperazine derivatives; an independent European patent describes cetirizine as that compound type.
IUPAC defines nido- as a nest-like open borane geometry and illustrates nido-pentaborane(9); independent cluster research uses nido-pentaborane as an exact standalone structural adjective.

The dictionary analyzes clorazepate as chlor- plus -azepate, while a pharmacokinetic study establishes that clorazepate yields desmethyldiazepam; the drug is a diazepam-related benzodiazepine carboxylate.
Historical embryology defines archoplasm and connects its first element to Greek archon, ruler; a scientific dictionary independently documents the same analysis and historical biological term.
WHO directly lists zaleplon under -plon; the FDA independently identifies it as a pyrazolopyrimidine hypnotic. Other functions and imidazopyrimidine examples were not separately verified.

entries.meaning: common bile duct, before a vowel (medicine)
entries.reason: A medical dictionary directly analyzes choledochectomy as choledoch- plus excision; Texas Education Agency materials independently define the exact operation as excision of the common bile duct.

entries.meaning: benzomorphan-related opioid agonists or antagonists (drug nomenclature)
entries.reason: WHO groups pentazocine under -azocine benzomorphan agonists or antagonists; an independent anaesthesia review describes pentazocine as a benzomorphan opioid agonist-antagonist.
WHO classifies sufentanil under the fentanyl-derived opioid analgesic -fentanil stem; the FDA identifies sufentanil as an opioid agonist and pain medicine.
WHO lists anileridine as a pethidine-derived analgesic under -eridine; PubChem independently documents its analgesic use and relationship in action to pethidine.

A scholarly work from the Macedonian Academy explains a historical Macedo-Bulgarian literary-language proposal as involving Macedonian dialects and Bulgarian; an independent Wilson Center publication also uses Macedo-Bulgarian for a linguistic grouping. This is a historical linguistic label for the region, not a claim about present language status.

A systematic Oxford catalogue of opioids explicitly assigns benzethidine to the WHO -ethidine stem for pethidine and derivatives; WHO's nomenclature classification relates -ethidine to analgesic pethidine derivatives.

entries.meaning: glucagon-like peptide analogue in drug names
entries.reason: WHO explicitly lists semaglutide under -glutide for glucagon-like peptide analogues; independent FDA substance data classifies semaglutide as a GLP-1 analogue. The WHO subsequently widened the stem to include agonists.

The Century Dictionary analyzes syphiloderm as syphilis plus Greek derma and defines a syphilitic skin lesion; an independent period medical textbook uses syphiloderm for a skin lesion of syphilis. This is historical medical vocabulary.

entries.meaning: peptide immunological agent for active immunization
entries.reason: WHO's stem book explicitly assigns tecemotide to -motide peptides used for active immunization; an independent oncology trial abstract describes tecemotide as an investigational lipopeptide cancer vaccine designed to induce an immune response.

entries.meaning: somatostatin receptor agonist or antagonist in peptide drug names
entries.reason: WHO lists octreotide under -reotide for somatostatin receptor agonists or antagonists; an independent pharmacology reference identifies octreotide as a somatostatin receptor agonist.

WHO's drug-stem book explicitly lists bexarotene under -arotene for arotinoid derivatives; an independent drug database classifies bexarotene within the same naming group and identifies its retinoid action.

Wiktionary directly analyzes arenophile as areno- plus -phile; an independent University of California Press book uses the English word for a sand collector, and a botanical journal independently uses the related adjective for sand-loving plants.
WHO defines -prostil for antiulcer prostaglandins and lists enprostil; an independent clinical paper identifies enprostil as a prostaglandin E2 derivative investigated as an antiulcer agent.
Independent medical sources define fasciocutaneous flaps as including fascia and skin; the source identifies fascio- as the fascia combining form. The example is surgical terminology.

entries.meaning: steroid or steroidlike drug outside the prednisolone family
entries.origin: pharmaceutical nomenclature ending from steroid names
entries.reason: WHO's drug stem table lists nandrolone under -olone steroids and distinguishes the USAN usage from prednisolone derivatives; PubChem independently identifies nandrolone as a testosterone-derived anabolic steroid. This does not imply that every word ending -olone shares that pharmacology.

entries.reason: The headword docosatriene is analyzed as docosa- meaning 22 plus triene; an independent Louisiana State University medical publication describes a docosatriene and relates its name to its carbon count. The scientific name is a single English term.

American Heritage directly analyzes corticotropin as cortico- plus -tropin; an international biochemical nomenclature recommendation calls it a pituitary tropic hormone and discusses -tropin for such hormones.

entries.origin: chiropter, bat, from Greek hand and wing
entries.reason: The New York Botanical Garden glossary defines chiropterophily as bat pollination; an independent scholarly review explicitly equates chiropterophily and bat pollination. This is the bat taxon combining element in botanical terminology.

entries.meaning: prednisone or prednisolone derivative in steroid drug names
entries.reason: WHO's stem book lists clobetasol under -betasol in the prednisone/prednisolone-derived steroid group; FDA product labeling separately identifies clobetasol as a prednisolone analogue.
A legal philosophy journal uses juridico-political for a law-and-politics sphere, while the source identifies juridico- with law. This is scholarly legal and political terminology.

entries.meaning: prednisone or prednisolone derivative in steroid drug names
entries.origin: pharmaceutical stem from methyl and prednisolone
entries.reason: WHO explicitly includes dexamethasone under -methasone among prednisone/prednisolone-derived steroids; an independent pharmacological structure comparison identifies dexamethasone as methyl-fluoroprednisolone.

entries.meaning: prednisone or prednisolone derivative in steroid drug names
entries.origin: pharmaceutical stem from methyl and prednisolone
entries.reason: WHO's stem book lists mometasone under the -metasone spelling in the prednisone/prednisolone-related corticosteroid section; NHS independently identifies mometasone as a corticosteroid. This is the exact form without h.

A university game-studies thesis explains ludonarrative as the conjunction of ludic gameplay and narrative; the game publisher Capcom independently uses and defines ludonarrative as interaction between gameplay and story.

entries.reason: Two independent libraries and a regional tourism organization use Bookapalooza for public events showcasing and promoting books and authors. The exact closed spelling is book plus -apalooza; this is the promotional-event sense rather than a general abundance sense.

The source defines teleio- as adult, fully grown; a peer-reviewed psychology study independently defines teleiophilia as a preference for sexually mature adults. This is a specialist research term, and attraction to adults is not itself classified as a disorder.

entries.meaning: neurokinin NK2 receptor antagonist in drug names
entries.reason: WHO's drug nomenclature book explicitly lists saredutant under -dutant as an NK2 receptor antagonist; an independently authored European patent likewise identifies saredutant among NK2 receptor antagonists.
WHO lists ifosfamide under the cyclophosphamide-group -fosfamide stem; the National Cancer Institute describes it as an alkylating cyclophosphamide analogue.
Wiktionary explicitly analyzes infundibulopelvic as infundibulo- plus pelvic; a urological study independently uses the term for an angle involving the renal infundibulum.
WHO places edelfosine among cytostatic -fosine compounds; independent cancer research describes its antitumor phospholipid character.

entries.meaning: serotonin receptor antagonists and partial agonists
entries.reason: WHO lists tegaserod under -serod serotonin receptor modulators; FDA independently identifies it as a serotonin-4 receptor agonist.

entries.meaning: underground water or cave habitat, associated with the underworld

Wiktionary analyzes tyrannophobia as tyranno- plus -phobia; an independent scholarly discussion defines the term in relation to fear of tyranny.
WHO lists dydrogesterone under -gesterone; independent research characterizes dydrogesterone as a progesterone-like progestogen.
Wiktionary defines Albano- for Albania; historical scholarship uses Albano-Yugoslav for diplomatic relations involving Albania and Yugoslavia.

entries.meaning: two added hydrogen atoms in chemical nomenclature
entries.reason: Wiktionary lists dihydrostreptomycin under dihydro-; the New England Journal of Medicine describes its preparation by adding one hydrogen molecule to streptomycin.
Wiktionary lists climograph as a derivative of climo-; the American Meteorological Society independently defines climograph as a climatic diagram.
WHO explicitly lists gonadorelin in the -relin group; an independent hospital endocrine protocol describes gonadorelin-induced pituitary LH and FSH release.

entries.meaning: acyl group derived from pristanic acid
entries.reason: ChEBI defines pristanoyl-CoA as the pristanic acid coenzyme-A thioester; independent biochemical research confirms the pristanic acid to pristanoyl-CoA relation.
WHO explicitly lists tesamorelin under -morelin for growth hormone releasing peptides; FDA identifies tesamorelin as a growth hormone-releasing factor analogue.
Wiktionary lists colliculothalamocortical under colliculo-; a neuroscience study independently describes the pathway beginning in the inferior colliculus.
WHO lists protirelin under -tirelin for thyrotropin-releasing hormone analogues; PubChem independently identifies protirelin as synthetic thyrotropin-releasing hormone.
The source defines Lebano- as pertaining to Lebanon; a US State Department document independently uses Lebano-Syrian for a joint statement involving Lebanon and Syria.
WHO lists raloxifene in the -oxifene subgroup of -ifene; the National Cancer Institute independently describes raloxifene as a selective estrogen receptor modulator.
Wiktionary analyzes hadal as had- plus -al on the surface and notes its borrowing from French Hadès; Collins independently defines hadal as the deep-ocean zone.
WHO lists enclomifene in the -mifene subgroup; the European Medicines Agency independently identifies it as an isomer of clomifene.
Wiktionary directly parses heptadecagon as heptadeca- plus -gon; an independent mathematics text defines it as a seventeen-sided polygon.

entries.meaning: tamoxifen-group antiestrogens or estrogen receptor modulators
entries.reason: WHO lists droloxifene in the -oxifene group; PubChem independently describes it as a tamoxifen derivative and selective estrogen receptor modulator.
Wiktionary analyzes octadecagon as octadeca- plus -gon; an independent university engineering dissertation calls it an eighteen-sided shape.
WHO directly lists exemestane under -mestane aromatase inhibitors; the FDA label independently identifies exemestane as an aromatase inhibitor.
The English dictionary analyzes tridecagon as trideca- plus -gon; an independent geometry text identifies a tridecagon as a thirteen-sided polygon.
WHO lists letrozole under -rozole aromatase inhibitors; the FDA independently identifies letrozole as an aromatase inhibitor. Its triazole structure covers this branch of the source class.
The source defines nonadeca- as nineteen; an independent geometry text identifies a nonadecagon as a polygon with nineteen sides, yielding an exact numerical formation.
The dictionary explicitly analyzes annuloplasty as annulo- plus -plasty; cardiology literature independently identifies it as repair of a cardiac annulus.
The English dictionary analyzes triskaidecagon as triskaideca- plus -gon; the University of Regina independently identifies the exact spelling as a thirteen-sided polygon.

entries.meaning: dual PPAR-alpha and PPAR-gamma agonists (drug nomenclature)
entries.reason: WHO lists aleglitazar among dual alpha/gamma PPAR agonists under -glitazar; an independent molecular profiling study demonstrates activation of both receptors.
A Smithsonian model bears the exact name tetrakaidekahedron and has fourteen faces; the source affix records tetrakaideka- as fourteen.

WHO directly lists rafoxanide under the -oxanide salicylanilide antiparasitic stem; the European Medicines Agency independently identifies it as a halogenated salicylanilide.

Collins traces odometer to Greek hodos, way, and metron; the Museo Galileo independently explains the term as road measurement. The homographic tooth-related sense is separate.
Oxford documents quadrophonic as a variant of quadraphonic and defines the four-channel meaning; independent broadcast terminology uses the exact spelling for four-channel reproduction.

entries.meaning: hepatitis C virus NS5A inhibitors (antiviral nomenclature)

The dictionary analyzes vexillology from flag-related Latin vexillum and -logy, equivalent to vexillo- plus -logy; the Flag Institute independently explains the meaning and origin.

entries.meaning: cannabinoid receptor agonist in drug names

entries.meaning: ribofuranyl derivative of the pyrazofurin type in drug names

entries.meaning: playful hip-hop-related word formation (informal African American slang)

The dictionary parses rufoferruginous as rufo- plus ferruginous and defines the rusty-red zoological color; an independent South African Museum zoological description uses the term.

Partridge’s etymological dictionary analyzes egolatrous as ego plus the -latrous of idolatrous, and identifies it among terms for self-worship.

entries.reason: The dictionary analyzes diskospondylitis as disko- plus spondylitis; the MSD Veterinary Manual independently defines it as inflammation of an intervertebral disk and adjacent vertebrae.

entries.origin: Back-formation from genome and related biological terms
entries.reason: Biology: the suffix -ome denotes a complete set; genome is explicitly identified as an example in both references. The earlier full-001 review addressed a different gloss and its individual rejected examples, which are not reused here.

entries.meaning: relating to a specified mode of living
entries.reason: Biology: -biotic denotes a mode of living; the American Heritage entry specifically gives endobiotic, and the source independently lists the same adjective. This establishes the previously held adjective sense and example.
The biological term ethogram records behavior and is analyzed as etho- representing ethology plus -gram; the behavior sense belongs with the existing Greek eth family.

entries.meaning: one who studies or specializes in a field
entries.reason: The suffix identifies a specialist or student of a field; cardiologist is explicitly given in both sources. It can be understood as a formative from -logy plus -ist rather than claiming a unique segmentation.
The Latin-derived prefix pene- means almost, and both dictionaries explicitly give peneplain as its example; it is the prevocalic variant pen- family already recorded.

Organic chemistry uses alk- for an aliphatic compound class; alkyl is explicitly cited for this element and independently traced to German Alk(ohol) plus -yl. The chemical sense is distinct from ordinary alkali. Collins traces alkyl to German Alk(ohol) plus -yl, supporting the link to the alcohol family.

entries.meaning: a crystal of a specified kind
entries.reason: Geology uses -cryst for a crystal: phenocryst is a conspicuous crystal and is explicitly analyzed as pheno- plus shortened crystal. The earlier hold concerned word-initial crystallize and does not establish that separate relation.

The form dromo- denotes running or movement, and both sources specifically connect it to dromomania. The earlier hold concerns the different terminal form -dromous in catadromous, which this decision does not reuse.

entries.origin: back-formation from qubit, from quantum and bit
entries.reason: Quantum computing uses qu- as a clipped combining form from qubit; qutrit denotes a quantum trit and is analyzed as qu- plus trit. Earlier exclusion concerned unrelated Latin antiquus, not the quantum sense.

entries.meaning: forms book format names based on the number of leaves per sheet
entries.reason: Bookbinding -mo forms a format name after twelve; Collins independently defines twelvemo as duodecimo, while the historical mo exclusion concerned fragments of more and most, an unrelated analysis.

The chemical combining form denotes phosphorus; phosphorochalcite is a copper phosphate mineral, confirming the phosphorus sense and initial combining form. Its variant phosphor- belongs to the existing phosphorus family.

entries.meaning: of or relating to the technicolor model in particle physics
entries.reason: Particle Data Group describes technipions in technicolor models; techni- denotes the model, a distinct sense from the older art or skill family and from the unresolved historical techni- item.

entries.meaning: a mathematical ordered collection of a specified number of terms
entries.origin: abstracted from quintuple and similar words
entries.reason: The reanalyzed suffix -tuple forms n-tuple, an ordered list of n elements in mathematics; its modern boundary is distinct from the original historical Latin multiplicative suffix.
Latin decem means ten and decemvir is analyzed as decem + vir. The prior hold was for an unsupported embedded use; this source explicitly marks initial position and supports the example.

entries.meaning: forms names of fully unsaturated four-membered nitrogen heterocycles
entries.reason: IUPAC nomenclature uses ete for the unsaturated four-membered ring in azete; PubChem gives azete and its ring structure. The old same-spelling English instance sense is unrelated.
Iridocyclitis is inflammation of the iris and ciliary body; independent medical and morphological sources support initial irido-. The old irid/irido review retains the iris sense.

entries.meaning: indicates attachment of polyethylene glycol to a drug
entries.reason: WHO identifies peg- in names for substances with polyethylene glycol, and NCI defines pegfilgrastim as filgrastim with polyethylene glycol attached. The former fix sense is distinct.

entries.meaning: indicates a three-carbon parent chain in organic chemistry
entries.origin: from propionic acid in chemical nomenclature
entries.reason: In chemical nomenclature prop- identifies a three-carbon parent chain, as in propane; earlier exclusion rejected the unrelated claim that prop alone means push or promote.

entries.meaning: indicates a racemic mixture in drug names
entries.reason: Racibuprofen is an attested name for racemic ibuprofen; the pharmacological article uses both hyphenated and solid forms, while AMA and IUPAC explain the rac descriptor.
Sonogram combines the sound element and -gram; NCI independently defines the medical image as produced using sound waves. This variant is linked to the existing Latin sound family.
The language authorities distinguish reciprocal or mutual action from the locative between and among sense, illustrated by interdependent and interact.
Almighty reflects Old English all plus mighty; al- represents the whole or complete sense. This Germanic component differs from the existing Latin al- toward and Greek al- other.

entries.origin: abbreviation of aldehyde in systematic nomenclature
entries.reason: Organic nomenclature uses -al to form aldehyde names: both IUPAC and Calgary explicitly identify ethanal as an example. This chemical suffix is distinct from adjectival and action-noun -al.

entries.meaning: a collective body of a specified class
entries.origin: Old English dōm, judgment and condition
entries.reason: Officialdom denotes officials collectively and is formed from official plus -dom; the collective sense differs from the existing domain or state gloss, while belonging to the same historical suffix family.

Arene denotes an aromatic hydrocarbon; Collins explicitly derives the name from ar(omatic) plus -ene, and ChEBI defines the chemical class. This chemical use is distinct from prior homonymous ar- senses.

entries.meaning: forms names of types of astronomical objects
entries.origin: clipped from star or stellar, on the model of quasar and pulsar
entries.reason: The astronomy ending -ar, modeled on quasar and pulsar and extracted from star, occurs in magnetar; NASA defines the resulting term as a magnetic neutron star.

entries.meaning: away, negative, destructive, or intensive force in older English word formation
entries.reason: The historical verb forcast means cast away and exemplifies the away sense of Old English for-; do not confuse it with forecast meaning predict.
Forfeit descends through French forfaire from Latin foris outside plus facere do; the Romance for- is separate from Germanic for- and its extended sense is doing amiss.

entries.meaning: forms variants of certain adverbs and prepositions without major change in meaning
entries.reason: Amongst is a variant of among with a surface -st ending; historically -s was an adverbial genitive and -t was added later. The relation records the reanalyzed ending, not a claim of original single-morpheme formation.

In the anatomical sense adrenal denotes at or near a kidney; both Collins and the National Cancer Institute explicitly analyze ad- as near plus renal. This spatial sense is linked to the existing Latin ad- family.

The anatomical suffix -ad denotes direction toward; both medical sources explicitly give cephalad as toward the head. This suffix derives from Latin ad and is distinct from the collective-number suffix.

entries.origin: clipping of intersex, ultimately Latin inter
entries.reason: Interphobia denotes prejudice against intersex people; inter- represents clipped intersex, a later sense distinct from the earlier between prefix.

entries.meaning: up or out; intensive verbal prefix
entries.reason: Arise historically combines Old English a- indicating up or out with rise; both historical sources identify the specific prefix. This Germanic verbal prefix is distinct from the existing Latin toward and Old English on senses.
Avert means turn away and derives from Latin ā-, a variant of ab- away, plus vertere. This Latin prefix is distinct from the existing toward and Old English on a- senses.
Anew derives from Old English of-niowe, literally of new; its prefix is the reduced Germanic preposition of and is historically distinct from Latin away and Old English on.

entries.meaning: intensifies the meaning of the base
entries.reason: Confirm descends from Latin con- with intensive force plus firmare strengthen; independent etymological references describe this historical prefix function.

entries.meaning: constructed or fictional in language and world creation
entries.origin: clipped from constructed, modeled on conlang
entries.reason: Conworld names a constructed fictional world; Cambridge documents its analogy with conlang, and the source identifies con- as the clipped constructed element in this specialist community.
Comic-Con is an attested comic-book convention; USPTO evidence explicitly identifies con as an event-name suffix for convention, a clipping distinct from the Latin prefix.
Aneal is an attested historical spelling of anneal, historically from Old English on- plus the verb meaning kindle; an- records its historical written variant.

entries.meaning: polysaccharide formed from a specified sugar
entries.reason: Glucan is a polymer of glucose; carbohydrate nomenclature forms such names by replacing the sugar ending -ose with -an.

entries.origin: clipped from supersymmetry, ultimately Latin super
entries.reason: A superpartner is a particle related to another by supersymmetry; particle-physics sources explicitly use this specialist formation.

Chicken historically contains a diminutive -en in the older bird name, as both sources explain. Modern chick is a later shortening, so the source’s chick plus -en construction is not presented as its historical derivation.

Vixen historically denotes a female fox and preserves a Germanic feminine ending -en with vowel and initial consonant changes; this is a historical relation, not a claim that modern fox simply concatenates with -en.

entries.meaning: indicates a carbon–carbon double bond in a chemical name
entries.origin: French -ène, variant of -ene before a vowel
entries.reason: Organic nomenclature uses internal -en- for a carbon–carbon double bond before the alcohol suffix: prop-2-en-1-ol is allyl alcohol and the locant identifies its double bond. The terminal e of -ene is elided before -ol. In unsaturated alcohol nomenclature the -en- element is internal before the alcohol ending -ol; Texas calls it an infix. The source label -en is retained, while combining_form describes this documented nonterminal placement.

entries.meaning: a collection of material associated with a person, place, or subject
entries.reason: Americana names collected objects and information associated with America; Merriam-Webster explicitly lists -ana as the collection suffix and Collins analyzes the word accordingly.

entries.meaning: a sweetened drink made from a specified fruit
entries.reason: Limeade names a fruit drink and is explicitly given as an example of beverage-forming -ade by independent dictionaries; this is distinct from the action suffix. The drink sense developed from the same Romance suffix family as the existing action/result -ade.
Paracolpitis is inflammation of connective tissue around the vagina; medical dictionaries document the surrounding tissue sense of this compound.
Paraphasia is abnormal speech involving inappropriate or incorrect words; the documented prefix denotes alteration from the expected form.
Paramilitary denotes an organization resembling or auxiliary to the military; the cited dictionary identifies para- as near or resembling.

entries.origin: Greek para, used in chemical nomenclature
entries.reason: Paradichlorobenzene is the 1,4 isomer of dichlorobenzene; para- names the opposite positions of its two ring substituents.
Paracord denotes parachute cord, a lightweight rope originally used in parachute lines; para- represents the clipped word parachute.

entries.meaning: disability sport or athletes with a disability
entries.reason: A para-athlete is an athlete with a disability; the attested hyphenated term uses para- in disability sport terminology.
Cellulolytic means able to break down cellulose; Merriam-Webster lists cellul- and cellulo- as cellulose combining forms with this example.

entries.origin: from ethyl, coined from ether plus -yl
entries.reason: Organic nomenclature uses eth- for a two-carbon parent chain, as in ethane; the form is historically taken from ethyl and ultimately ether, not the Greek behavior root eth.

Internet slang uses shitpost for a type of online post, with the final component post; dictionaries document the compound and its noun meaning. The form extends the existing posting family to online messages.

Bi-curious refers to curiosity about bisexuality and is formed from clipped bi plus curious; this distinct sexuality-related use derives historically from bisexual, rather than meaning exactly two people or genders.

The source dictionary explicitly assigns anis- unequal to anisodont; the dentistry dictionary defines anisodont as having unequal teeth. This Greek element belongs with existing aniso- unequal, distinct from the unrelated anise root.
Panphobia in this source sense denotes prejudice against pansexual people, so pan- is a clipping of pansexual; this is distinct from the unrelated fear-of-everything sense.

entries.meaning: forms names of alcohols and some phenols
entries.origin: chemical suffix from alcohol or phenol
entries.reason: The chemical suffix -ol denotes alcohols and sometimes phenols; butanol denotes a four-carbon alcohol and illustrates the alcohol scope of the source.

entries.meaning: forms humorous names of fictitious afflictions
entries.reason: Senioritis humorously describes reduced student motivation as a fictitious affliction, extending the medical -itis suffix; it does not denote inflammation.
Printed chori- means chorion or chorionic and is a variant of existing chorio-; chorionic means relating to the chorion, separate from the adjacent chori- meaning apart.
Omophagia denotes eating raw flesh; the first element is Greek ōmos raw, distinct from the unrelated shoulder element.

entries.origin: Greek toxikon arrow poison, from toxon bow
entries.reason: Toxophore denotes the toxic part of a toxin molecule; toxo- refers to toxin, distinct from its homograph meaning bow or archery.

entries.meaning: suitable to; having the quality of
entries.reason: Seasonable means suitable to a season or time; the noun-derived -able formation expresses suitability rather than passive ability.

entries.meaning: giving or causing a specified effect
entries.reason: Pleasurable means giving pleasure and is formed from pleasure plus -able; this effect-producing use differs from passive capability.
Taxable means subject to taxation; dictionaries explicitly use this word for the obligation or subject-to use of -able.

entries.origin: Greek notos, south wind and south
entries.reason: The taxonomic name Nototherium means southern beast; the original dictionary identifies noto- as the southern element from Greek notos. This is unrelated to the separately existing noto- meaning back.
Independent botanical sources analyze helophyte as helo- marsh plus -phyte plant. This is a different Greek homonym from helo- nail.
Algotherapy denotes the therapeutic use of algae or seaweed; its algo- element derives from alga, distinct from Greek algos pain.

The dictionary distinguishes sulph- in sulfanilamide-derived drug names from the sulfur element. PubChem identifies sulphacetamide as a spelling of sulfacetamide and a sulfanilamide derivative; this variant joins the existing sulpha drug family.

entries.meaning: forms names of electromagnetic units in the centimeter-gram-second system
entries.reason: In the centimeter-gram-second electromagnetic system, ab- forms the corresponding unit name, including abvolt. This scientific prefix is a shortening of absolute and differs from Latin ab- away.

entries.meaning: succinic acid; derived from succinic acid
entries.origin: Latin succinum, amber, via succinic acid
entries.reason: Chemical succin- names succinic-acid derivatives; same historical amber family but a distinct scientific sense.

entries.meaning: other diastereoisomer of a named amino acid
entries.origin: Greek allos other, in chemical nomenclature
entries.reason: Alloisoleucine is a diastereoisomer of isoleucine; IUPAC explicitly documents allo- as a stereochemical nomenclature prefix.

entries.meaning: experiencing sexual or romantic attraction; not asexual or aromantic
entries.origin: Greek allos other, reinterpreted in sexuality terminology
entries.reason: Allosexual denotes a person who is not asexual in current identity terminology; allo- has developed a specific contrastive sense in this context.
Antumbra names the region beyond the umbral shadow; the term contains ant- as the prevocalic variant of Latin ante before.

entries.origin: shortened from arc of a circle, ultimately Latin arcus
entries.reason: Arcsine denotes the inverse sine function; the mathematical prefix arc- historically names the arc whose sine has the specified value.

Acroyoga blends acrobatics and yoga; acro is a clipping of acrobatics, not the spatial height sense used literally. The clipped form is historically connected to the existing acro- family through acrobatics.
Aliethmoid refers to a lateral or wing part of the ethmoid region; ali- derives from Latin ala wing and is unrelated to the existing ali- other root.
The adjective all-powerful uses the English prefix all- with powerful to express complete power. The form is cognate with the existing al- all in almighty, but differs from the Greek all- other root.

entries.meaning: of or relating to; historical spelling of -al
entries.origin: historical English spelling of -al, from Latin -alis
entries.reason: The historical spelling lineall corresponds to lineal, with obsolete -all representing adjectival -al. It is a spelling variant of the existing Latin-derived relational suffix, not the unrelated all meaning other.
Pharmacology references identify -ac as a drug-name stem for acetic acid anti-inflammatory agents, including diclofenac; this is separate from Greek adjectival -ac.
Acupuncture derives from Latin acus needle plus puncture; this needle sense shares the existing sharp-point family.
Adenotonsillectomy combines adeno- adenoid with tonsil and excision, a tissue-specific clipping historically related to gland.
The grammar identifies leafage as a collective noun formed with -age, matching the collection sense.
The suffix -age denotes a state in bondage, which the prior review correctly separated from action of a verb.
A vicarage is a residence and the sources explicitly identify -age as the place-forming suffix.
The suffix -age denotes a charge in postage; the old review separated this fee sense from the action of a verb.
Percentage means a rate per hundred and is historically formed from percent plus -age.

entries.origin: Greek arkhē and arkhein, via Latin and French
entries.reason: An archvillain is an outstandingly villainous person; arch- is an established intensifier, as independently described by linguistic references.
A poetaster is an inferior poet; Latin -aster is a pejorative suffix and is unrelated to the Greek star word aster.

entries.origin: shortened from automatic, ultimately Greek autos self
entries.reason: Autofocus is automatic focusing in photography; the first element represents automatic rather than the reflexive self in this formation.

entries.origin: shortened from automobile, ultimately Greek autos self
entries.reason: An autocar is a self-propelled vehicle; Oxford describes auto- as a clipped automobile element meaning motor-powered in vehicle names.

entries.origin: shortened from automobile, ultimately Greek autos self
entries.reason: Autocross is a type of motor racing; auto- represents automobile in this compound according to dictionary evidence.
Angeball names the style of football associated with coach Ange Postecoglou; the productive -ball element identifies a style of play.

entries.meaning: person characterized by a quality, often disparaging
entries.reason: Goofball denotes a foolish or silly person; linguistic commentary identifies -ball as a productive informal person-labeling suffix.
Botanical amphivasal uses amphi- around for xylem completely surrounding phloem.
Chemical nomenclature uses -ane for saturated parent hydrides, including hydrocarbons such as methane; this is independent of adjectival -ane.
Behead means deprive of the head; sources explicitly identify this historical be- as a privative prefix meaning off or away.

entries.meaning: most recent common, in ancestor terminology
entries.origin: blend of Greek kainos recent and koinos common
entries.reason: Cenancestor names a most recent common ancestor; a phylogenetic terminology study explicitly explains cen- as combining recent and common.
A cenotaph is a monument or tomb without the remains; ceno- denotes empty, distinct from the homographic recent and common forms.
A cenobite lives in a monastic community; ceno- is the written variant of coeno- common in the term.

The antielectron is the electron’s antimatter counterpart, the positron. The specialist anti- prefix identifies an antiparticle rather than temporal precedence and is historically related to anti- opposed.

entries.meaning: person habitually or excessively in a specified condition
entries.origin: French -ard, from Germanic hard meaning bold
entries.reason: Drunkard contains the pejorative person suffix -ard after drunk. The suffix derives through French from a Germanic element meaning bold or hard, and is unrelated to Latin ard- burn.
The scientific apo- without sense occurs in apogamy, plant development without gamete fusion.
The botanical apoplast is the space external to the plasma membrane; apo- identifies the outside compartment.
Coloration includes the state or arrangement of colors and illustrates the state sense of -ation.
Medical terminology defines auro- ear, and auropalpebral describes a blink response to auditory stimulation, distinct from auro- gold.

entries.meaning: complement with respect to a fixed angle
entries.origin: from complement, historically Latin com- together
entries.reason: Colatitude is the complement of latitude to ninety degrees; co- denotes a complementary quantity in mathematical and astronomical usage.
A colimit is the categorical dual of a limit; mathematics sources explicitly describe co- as marking a dual construction.

entries.meaning: assistant or secondary person in a role
entries.origin: Latin co- together, extended to an auxiliary role
entries.reason: A copilot is a second pilot assisting the pilot in command; co- denotes an auxiliary role in this aviation term.

entries.meaning: containing a cyanide or nitrile group
entries.origin: from cyanogen, ultimately Greek kyanos dark blue
entries.reason: Cyanoacrylate contains a cyano or nitrile group; cyano- is the chemical group name rather than a statement about color.

entries.meaning: having, characterized by, resembling, or affected by a specified thing or action
entries.reason: Lobate means having lobes, with adjectival -ate marking the specified characteristic. This adjective-forming suffix derives from Latin -atus and is distinguished from the existing verb-forming sense.

entries.meaning: material resulting from or affected by a process
entries.origin: from Latin -atus participial adjectives used as nouns
entries.reason: Diffusate is material that has diffused through a membrane; noun-forming -ate marks the result or affected material of the process. It is distinct from the chemical salt-naming suffix.

entries.meaning: forms names of certain acid-derived anions, salts, or esters
entries.origin: New Latin -atum, nominal use of Latin adjectival -atus
entries.reason: Acetate is a chemical anion or acid-derived salt group named with -ate; independent chemical nomenclature sources explicitly identify this ending. The meaning is restricted to the nomenclature use.

entries.meaning: office, rank, domain, institution, governing group, or associated state
entries.reason: Emirate combines emir and noun-forming -ate and can denote an emir’s rank or office. This office and institution suffix comes from Latin abstract noun -atus.

entries.origin: short for biological, from Greek bios life
entries.reason: Bioparent refers to a biological parent, and bio- here is a clipped form of biological indicating genetic relationship. It is connected through biological to the existing Greek life family but has a narrower interpersonal meaning.

entries.origin: from borne, past participle of bear
entries.reason: Fear-borne in a published ecology paper describes killing caused by fear; the source dictionary records this causal sense of -borne. It is distinguished from physical transport and linked to the same bear-derived family.

entries.meaning: associated with the fictional superhero Batman
entries.source_entry: Bat- associated with the fictional superhero Batman
entries.reason: The Batman franchise uses Bat- to form names of its character-specific objects, including Batmobile.

entries.origin: Middle English bel-, from French bel
entries.reason: Historical bel- denotes kinship in beldame grandmother; it derives from the same French bel as the existing fine sense.
The clipped -bot denotes an automated system; chatbot combines chat with bot for a conversational computer program.

entries.meaning: four carbon atoms in a parent chain
entries.source_entry: but- four carbon atoms in a parent chain
entries.reason: Chemical nomenclature uses but- for a four-carbon chain, as in butane, historically deriving the element from butyric acid.
In online subculture truecel is a self-described authentic involuntary celibate, using -cel as a subtype label.

entries.meaning: person characterized by a stated trait; humorous internet slang
entries.source_entry: -cel person characterized by a stated trait; humorous internet slang
entries.reason: The humorous online term wordcel extends -cel beyond celibacy to a person identified with verbal skills.

entries.meaning: intensive prefix used with an already negative verb
entries.origin: Latin dis- apart, developed an intensifying use
entries.reason: Disannul means annul rather than reverse annulment; historical dictionaries explicitly characterize this dis- as intensive.

entries.meaning: bad or abnormal, as a variant spelling of dys-
entries.reason: Disfunction is a documented variant spelling of dysfunction; its dis- represents the abnormal-function sense of dys- rather than ordinary reversal.

entries.origin: Old Norse byr, dwelling or town
entries.reason: Bylaw historically combines Old Norse by town or settlement with law. This element is unrelated to the existing English by meaning near or aside, and also occurs in place names as a final component.

entries.meaning: organism dispersed by a specified agent or method
entries.origin: Greek khorein, to move or spread
entries.reason: A zoochore is a plant whose reproductive parts are dispersed by animals. The biological -chore ending indicates a plant dispersed in a specified way and is unrelated to the existing chore- dance root.

entries.meaning: heterogeneous geographic unit or mosaic of ecological habitats
entries.reason: An ecochore is a landscape unit formed from a characteristic mosaic of ecotopes. The territorial -chore is distinct from both dispersal -chore and the unrelated dance root.

entries.origin: short for cryonics, from Greek kryos cold
entries.reason: A cryopatient is a person undergoing or having undergone cryonics procedures. In this specialist compound cryo- refers to cryonics, a cold-preservation practice connected to the existing Greek cold family.

entries.meaning: relating to cisgender people or identity
entries.origin: Latin cis on this side, via cisgender
entries.source_entry: cis- relating to cisgender people or identity
entries.reason: Cisnormativity combines cis- for cisgender identity with normativity to name expectations that privilege cis people.

entries.source_entry: copro- obscenity; obscene language or behavior
entries.reason: In psychology coprolalia denotes involuntary obscene speech; copro- extends its original excrement sense to verbal obscenity.

entries.meaning: vehicle or vessel of a specified kind
entries.origin: English craft, vessel, from craft skill
entries.source_entry: -craft vehicle or vessel of a specified kind
entries.reason: Aircraft combines air with craft vessel, a vehicle sense historically related to craft as skill.
Hermitcraft names a Minecraft multiplayer server; -craft is abstracted from the game title for themed servers and modifications.

entries.origin: Greek endon, prevocalic form of endo-
entries.reason: Endarteritis is inflammation of an artery inner lining; end- is the documented prevocalic variant of endo- within.

entries.meaning: enantiomeric counterpart of a natural product
entries.reason: Ent-kaurene names the enantiomer of kaurene; IUPAC explicitly recognizes ent- as an enantiomeric chemical nomenclature prefix.

entries.origin: Greek entos, prevocalic form of ento-
entries.reason: Entoptic refers to visual phenomena originating within the eye; ent- is the prevocalic variant of ento- within.

entries.source_entry: cross- against an expected side; opposing
entries.reason: To cross-vote is to vote against one’s usual party or bloc, illustrating opposition to an expected side.

entries.meaning: across or involving multiple groups or domains
entries.source_entry: cross- across or involving multiple groups or domains
entries.reason: Cross-cultural describes interactions involving more than one culture, extending the crossing sense to domains.

entries.origin: English cross, contrasted with the usual arrangement
entries.source_entry: cross- alternative to a usual configuration
entries.reason: Fiddlers cross-tune an instrument using an alternative tuning instead of the standard arrangement.

entries.meaning: cross-country racing over an obstacle course
entries.source_entry: -cross cross-country racing over an obstacle course
entries.reason: Motocross denotes cross-country motorcycle racing and contains cross shortened from cross-country.

entries.meaning: given-name formative used in African American naming
entries.source_entry: De- given-name formative used in African American naming
entries.reason: DeAndre is a personal name formed using De-; scholarly and naming references attest this productive given-name element.

entries.meaning: distinctive language or jargon of a group
entries.reason: Journalese denotes the characteristic language of journalism; -ese forms nouns for a professional or group-specific style.

entries.origin: shortened form of Europe or Euro-
entries.reason: Eurasian combines Europe and Asia; Eur- is the documented prevocalic form of Euro-, distinct from Greek eur- wide.

entries.origin: abstracted from cryptography or cryptogram, from Greek kryptos hidden
entries.reason: Encrypt denotes conversion to a cipher, and the final crypt element is documented as abstracted from words of cryptography. It is historically related to the Greek hidden root but has a specific coding use.

entries.origin: short for cryptographic, from Greek kryptos hidden
entries.reason: Cryptosystem is a contraction of cryptographic system. In this technical use crypto- represents cryptography, historically derived from the existing Greek hidden family.

entries.origin: short for cryptocurrency, from cryptographic currency
entries.reason: A cryptocoin is a unit of cryptocurrency; crypto- in this financial context refers to cryptocurrency and is a later extension of the cryptography family.

entries.origin: Greek kyklos circle; applied to the encircling ciliary body
entries.reason: In ophthalmology cycloplegia is paralysis of the ciliary body, with cyclo- denoting that structure; the specific anatomical sense shares its Greek circular origin with the existing cyclo family.

entries.meaning: containing deuterium in place of hydrogen
entries.origin: from deuterium, from Greek deuteros second
entries.reason: Deuterobenzene is a benzene form containing deuterium; the chemical prefix deutero- specifies replacement by the hydrogen isotope and comes from deuterium, ultimately named from Greek second.

entries.origin: short for dinoflagellate, from Greek dine whirling
entries.reason: A dinocyst is a dinoflagellate cyst; here dino- is a shortening of dinoflagellate, whose name contains Greek dino- whirling. This organismal use is distinct from the original rotation sense.
Eddy is historically analyzed as a back-flow of water with Old English ed- back; the prefix survives here in a fossilized compound and is unrelated to Latin ed- eat.

entries.meaning: having or characterized by a specified feature
entries.origin: Old English adjectival -od, related to the weak participial ending
entries.reason: Horned means having horns and uses the derivational adjective suffix -ed on the noun horn, distinct in function from the regular verbal inflection.

entries.meaning: person who performs an action or is associated with something
entries.origin: extension of Anglo-French recipient -ee from Latin participial -atus
entries.reason: A standee is a person who stands, with active -ee attached to an intransitive verb; this is a documented extension of the recipient suffix but differs in semantic role.

entries.meaning: small or familiar version of the named thing
entries.origin: variant of the English diminutive -y or -ie
entries.reason: A bootee is a small boot or soft infant shoe, formed from boot with diminutive -ee. This suffix is associated with pet-name -y rather than the homographic person suffix.

entries.meaning: digit nine in systematic chemical element names
entries.reason: Ununennium is the systematic temporary name for element 119, built from un-un-enn-ium; enn represents the digit nine. It occurs inside numeric element names, so the combining-form classification reflects its documented position.

entries.source_entry: e- electronic; digital or internet based
entries.reason: E-mail is electronic mail and illustrates the modern digital e- prefix, unrelated to Latin e- out.
E-stop abbreviates emergency stop in safety equipment terminology, with e- denoting emergency.
An e-bike is an electrically powered or assisted bicycle, with e- standing for electric.
An eSIM is an embedded subscriber identity module, and e- stands for embedded in this technical term.
